newsitem.title: USA: NYS Republicans got $1 mln from bond firms-senator.
newsitem.headline: NYS Republicans got $1 mln from bond firms-senator.

text.p: A New York State Senator said Wednesday that state Republicans got almost $1 million in campaign contributions in 1995 and 1996 from municipal bond firms that were awarded profitable underwriting contracts.
The firms that made the contributions were selected as underwriters for 248 municipal bond sales in fourth quarter 1996, according to a report by State Sen. Franz Leichter, D-Manhattan.
Leichter in early April sought to force the state senate to release from committee several campaign finance and election reform bills, efforts that the Republican-led Senate has blocked.

The state senator accused the underwriters of violating the spirit if not the letter of Securities and Exchange Commission rule G-37, which he said prohibits -- with some clearly defined exceptions -- firms and some of the employees from making political contributions to public officials who oversee municipal bond sales within two years of getting any negotiated municipal securities business in that state.

While Gov. George Pataki did not get direct contributions from the firms, the state senator said the Republican governor was aided by the almost $1 million in donations that underwriters gave Republican comittees.

Those committees were the National Republican Senatorial Committee, two bodies set up to campaign for the approval of the 1996 Clean Water/Clean Air Bond Act, and the Republican State Committee's "housekeeping" account.
When asked about the state senator's report by reporters in Albany, Pataki attacked restrictions fund-raising by underwriting officials who make individual contributions.

"I think first of all that the ban is something that restricts people from being able to donate, who would like to be supportive of the policies and the efforts we are making, and I mean specifically individuals who work on Wall Street, who are supportive of our policies and I think that's unfortunate," Pataki said.

The National Republican Senatorial Committee is a federal group controlled by U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato, R-New York, which raised more than $500,000 in "soft money" contributions from underwriters in the 1996 election year, and provided Pataki's campaign with $1.9 million, Leichter said.
The two bond act committees, which were controlled by Pataki and D'Amato, raised nearly $300,000 from 13 underwriters.

The state senator said published polls showed that advertisements paid for by the bond act committees helped boost both Pataki's and D'Amato's approval ratings. A spokesman for D'Amato was not immediately available to comment.

Leichter added that the Republican State Committee, which raised several thousand dollars from underwriters to its housekeeping account, which lets firms give unlimited sums, spent over $250,000 in housekeeping funds on political consultants in 1996, including D'Amato and and Pataki consultants, as well as fund raising events hosted by Pataki.
